statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress firms one point to 53 in the elevated band: a senior Iranian official said Monday's Salalah meeting is not expected to produce a signed Hormuz agreement, Bahrain will not attend, and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays shut with no published repair timeline. Confidence is 87, because the index level, VIX, Treasury yields, crude, the FOMC pricing and the seven-day calendar were each re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly three hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot in the forward window can contain the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures. Third, the unresolved items are supply-side and policy-side rather than structural: the shut East-West pipeline, the Houthi position at Bab el-Mandeb and a live FOMC week are all carried in Stress, which alone does not change the mapped state. No danger window is published, because narrow evidence-based windows are preferred and no hour inside a closed market qualifies.
headline: Twenty-three hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, while a senior Iranian official says Monday's Salalah meeting will not produce a signed Hormuz agreement and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut; CME FedWatch put a 25 basis point increase near 87% after Friday's CPI, up from about 69% before the release.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend, and was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX is 15.84, down 11.21% from 17.84, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

Two items changed materially since the previous hour, and both were verified directly. First, the rate-decision pricing carried in earlier assessments was stale. The Friday market wrap reports CME FedWatch at an 87% probability of a 25 basis point increase on 16 September after the CPI release, up from about 69% beforehand; a separate 9 September piece had the same measure above 60%, with Kalshi at 57% and Polymarket at 49%. The hike is therefore largely priced, which moves the residual uncertainty toward the projections and the press conference rather than the decision itself. Second, a senior Iranian official said Monday's meeting in Salalah, called at Oman's initiative with GCC states and Iraq, is not expected to yield a signed Hormuz agreement, and Bahrain said it will not attend until diplomatic ties with Tehran are restored. That trims the near-term de-escalation optionality which had been letting Stress decay through the day.

The supply channel is otherwise unchanged. Saudi Arabia's 745-mile East-West pipeline, which moves between 4% and 5% of global oil supplies and serves as the bypass around the blocked Strait of Hormuz, remains shut after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory late in the week; the energy ministry has described safety assessment work and published no restoration date, and an Iraqi commander was dismissed after the origin was confirmed. Houthi forces hold Perim island, Mocha and Dhubab, completing effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb gateway serving Yanbu, and the IEA reported Saudi crude supply at its lowest in more than three decades while cutting its 2026 demand outlook. Against that, President Trump repeated on Saturday that the war would end after the November midterms and that oil would fall sharply, and President Pezeshkian replied that Iran will not yield. That exchange is rhetorical, with no verified transmission into pricing.

August CPI, released Friday, rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over the year, matching expectations, while core rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above forecast, with the core annual rate easing to 2.4%. Equities rallied anyway as crude gave back part of the week's gain, breaking a four-session losing streak, though all three major indexes still finished the shortened week lower. Next week supplies the scheduled catalysts: Retail Sales and the FOMC decision with projections both land on 16 September, the Chair's press conference follows, and the index faces its own mechanics with roughly $15.5 billion of estimated passive flow around the 18 September rebalance close. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 18:49 UTC and is now about 97 minutes old with collectionStatus partial and its calendar section unavailable, so it is treated as stale under the inherited contract and is not relied upon materially in this assessment; the independent research above stands on its own.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 20:00 UTC on 11 September to 19:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in the U.S. afternoon that followed Friday's CPI print, with Tail at 13 in mixed mode and Stress in the high band at 72 as the event decayed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final twenty-three slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell from 72 to a 50 trough by 17:00 UTC and has since firmed back to 52 as weekend supply and diplomatic headlines accumulated. Confidence stayed between 85 and 89 throughout. No slot in the window reached the 20-point watch band, so every published action was EA_ON and every status green.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly three hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps gradually to a ceiling of 15 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Every slot stays inside the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published. Stress traces a shallow 50 to 54 path, easing through the quiet overnight hours and firming into Sunday afternoon as Monday's Salalah meeting and a live FOMC week approach. Confidence decays from 87 to 80 purely through the ageing of marks that cannot be refreshed while venues are shut. The mode stays normal until the final four slots, where it turns mixed because a reopen can resolve in either direction from a frozen reference.
